## Verdict

missing

## Bearer

PhoneNavigator — app-phone/src/main/java/com/mgilli/hyroxtracker/ui/navigation/PhoneNavigator.kt

## Trigger

The activity being recreated after process death (MainActivity.onCreate, savedInstanceState) — nothing observes it

## Today

PhoneNavigator is a `@Singleton` holding `backStack` as a plain
`mutableListOf<PhoneDestination>()`, seeded with `PhoneDestination.RaceList`
on construction. MainActivity.onCreate receives `savedInstanceState: Bundle?`
but never reads or writes it, and nothing in the codebase calls
`SavedStateHandle`, `onSaveInstanceState` or `rememberSaveable` for the
navigator's stack. When the process is recreated — after the OS reclaims
memory in the background or the app is relaunched — Hilt provides a fresh
`PhoneNavigator` instance, whose `backStack` is reinitialised to
`[RaceList]` alone: whatever screen the user was on is lost and the app
opens on the race list.

## Expected

The back stack PhoneNavigator holds is written to a persisted saved state
(e.g. through a `SavedStateHandle` or an equivalent instance-state bundle)
whenever it changes, and restored from it when the navigator is
constructed, so that reopening the app resumes on the destination the user
last saw instead of always on `PhoneDestination.RaceList`. Restoring
`PhoneDestination.RaceDetail(raceId)` requires the `raceId` to be
serialisable in that saved state; the other destinations
(`Profile`, `PasteResult`, `ImportPreview`, `PasteError`) carry no
parameters and restore directly. Note that `ImportPreview` and
`PasteError` are read as one-time snapshots of `PasteResultViewModel`'s
in-memory `uiState` (see MainActivity's `PhoneApp` composable) — that
state is not itself persisted, so restoring the stack to either of those
two destinations across a process death would need that snapshot to
survive too, or those two destinations excluded from what is restored.
